name: fixed_priority
why: the pointer never advances, so requester 0 always wins (starvation)

name: reset_pointer_zero
why: after reset requester 1, not requester 0, has highest priority

name: regrant_same_requester
why: the search starts at the last winner, so a busy requester keeps the grant

name: data_select_off_by_one
why: a grant to requester 1 writes requester 2's data

name: binary_grant
why: grant is the binary winner index instead of one-hot

name: write_first_bypass
why: a same-edge read returns the new write data instead of the old contents
replace: rd_data <= (wr_en && wr_addr == rd_addr) ? wr_data : mem[rd_addr]; // read_first

name: write_ignores_enable
why: idle cycles write zero to entry 0

name: reset_keeps_memory
why: reset clears rd_data but not the stored entries

name: asynchronous_regfile_reset
why: an off-edge reset pulse clears the register file
replace: always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin // regfile_clock

name: top_read_address_miswired
why: the integration wires requester 0's address to the read port
